To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) The effect of thermal shape fluctuations on several nuclear observables is important.

the inclusion of thermal fluctuations in the description of the superfluid to non-superfluid and deformed to spheroidal shape transitions leads to a decrease of the critical temperature for these transitions and a washing out of their signatures in several observables.

the thermal shape fluctuations in the description of the hot nucleus $^{152}$Gd are important and that the new values of the critical temperature for the shape transition are closer to the experimental ones than the ones found in the plain FTHF-B theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the description of hot and deformed nuclei, in the framework of the FTHFB model, including the thermal effects of fluctuations in the quadruple degree of freedom.
the study of the effects of the thermal fluctuations of the quadrupole deformation on the properties of the nuclear system at finite temperature.
the study of the effect of thermal shape fluctuations in the description of the hot nucleus, in the context of the FTHFB model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FTHFB theory is a powerful tool to study the thermal shape transition, provided that the thermal fluctuations are properly included.
the thermal shape fluctuation effects are not negligible in the description of nuclear properties at finite temperature.
the inclusion of shape fluctuations in the description of the hot nucleus reduces substantially the effect of temperature on the nuclear observables, but not completely suppresses the effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inclusion of shape fluctuations is essential to get a realistic description of nuclear properties at finite temperature.
the FTHFB theory is a good starting point for the description of the thermal shape transitions in heavy nuclei.
thermal shape fluctuations are important in the description of nuclear properties and they should be included in any model that aims to describe the behavior of nuclei at finite temperatures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thermal shape fluctuations have to be considered in order to get a realistic description of hot deformed nuclei.
the thermal shape fluctuations should be taken into account in the study of the nuclear properties at finite temperatures.
the Landau prescription for shape fluctuations should be taken into account when analyzing the behavior of nuclear observables with temperature, specially for temperatures close to $T_c$.
